events.text: Someone is breaking through the Void. Far below, on the highest mountain of {pw_world}, {pw_vb_name}, {pw_vb_from}, sits in the snow with their eyes closed and pushes on the ceiling of the world as if it were a door. The whole sky of {pw_world} creaks. Nobody has done this before. The lightning is yours to send, and how much of it.

choices.text: Look closely at them before you decide

effects.log: You look. Their breath, their bones, the Dao in them: {pw_vb_dao}. Whatever you send, you will send it knowing.

choices.text: Gather the storm, and wait

effects.log: The clouds over the mountain thicken and turn slowly, like a wheel. In {pw_world} the farmers bring the animals in.

events.text: A bell nobody rang sounds in every temple of {pw_world} at once. The priests run out into the courtyards and look up: the sky over the north is cracking like ice on a pond in spring, and in the middle of the cracks sits {pw_vb_name}. Someone is breaking through the Void. Every one of them knows it will be you who answers.

choices.text: Answer the bell with thunder, far off

effects.log: You let the thunder roll somewhere over the sea, a long way off. A warning. The priests fall to their knees.

choices.text: Let the bells ring on, and think

effects.log: The bells ring all night. You weigh {pw_vb_name} the way a smith weighs a blade before the quench.

events.text: For a thousand years nobody in {pw_world} has risen higher than the world you made allows. Now {pw_vb_name}, {pw_vb_from}, has, and stands at the very top of it with nowhere left to climb but through. Someone is breaking through the Void. The Dao in them is {pw_vb_dao}. The test of heaven is yours to give.

choices.text: Be proud of them, a little

effects.log: You made the mountain and the snow and the sky. You did not make {pw_vb_name}. They made themselves. You find you are proud.

choices.text: Remember that heaven must test them

effects.log: A heaven that opens for anyone is not a heaven. You roll the first of the lightning between your fingers.

choices.text: Ask yourself what you want them for

effects.log: A servant, a rival, a story for the temples. You do not like how quickly the answers come.

events.text: The lightning comes down on {pw_vb_name} like summer rain. They open their eyes, a little surprised, and stand up into it, and walk up the light as if it were a stair. The Void parts for them with a sound like a sigh, and then they are gone out of {pw_world}, wherever the ones who leave a world go.

choices.text: Watch them go

effects.log: You watch until the last of the light closes. Somewhere beyond your sky, {pw_vb_name} is beginning again.

choices.text: Wonder if you were too gentle

effects.log: The priests say the god was kind. You wonder if the god only misjudged them. Next time you will look harder.

events.text: It is over before the people of {pw_world} have finished looking up. {pw_vb_name} takes your lightning on one shoulder, shrugs it off, and steps through the Void as if through a curtain. On the mountain there is only a warm patch in the snow, and the shape of someone who sat there for a long time.

choices.text: Let the world tell it its own way

effects.log: In a hundred years the story will say they flew up on a crane. You let it.

choices.text: Send one more roll of thunder, for the look of it

effects.log: The thunder rolls after them, too late. The temples hear it and are satisfied.

events.text: {pw_vb_name} was ready for much more than you sent. You can see it in the way they stand afterwards, at the edge of the open Void, looking back down at {pw_world} with something like disappointment, before they bow once to the empty sky and go.

choices.text: Bow back

effects.log: You bow back, though they cannot see it. The sky over the mountain clears in a single breath.

choices.text: Turn away before they finish bowing

effects.log: You turn away. It is not their fault that they did not need you.

events.text: You send too much. You know it the moment it leaves your hand, and it cannot be called back. The lightning comes down on the mountain white and silent, and the thunder after it shakes the snow off every peak in {pw_world}. When the cloud clears, there is a black circle in the snow, and in the middle of it a little grey ash.

choices.text: Go down and gather the ash yourself

effects.log: You go down in no shape at all and gather {pw_vb_name} in your hands. You scatter them over the valley they came from.

choices.text: Do not look away from it

effects.log: You make yourself look at the black circle for a long time. A god should know the weight of its own hand.

events.text: For three days the temples of {pw_world} hang white banners. The people climb the mountain in a long line to leave rice cakes and paper flowers in the black circle where {pw_vb_name}, {pw_vb_from}, sat to break the Void. The priests say heaven is just. Nobody says it loudly.

choices.text: Send a soft rain on the mourners

effects.log: A soft rain falls on the line of mourners. Some of them take it for tears. You do not correct them.

choices.text: Stay silent

effects.log: You stay silent. Silence, the priests will learn, is also an answer.

events.text: There is a moment, as your lightning falls, when {pw_vb_name} opens their eyes and looks straight up at you. Not afraid. Only surprised, as if they had expected something else from you. Then the light takes them, and {pw_world} is a little smaller than it was this morning.

choices.text: Carve their name on the mountain

effects.log: Their name is in the rock the next morning, cut deeper than any chisel could. Pilgrims will touch it for ten thousand years.

choices.text: Promise to read the next one better

effects.log: You make the promise to nobody. The black circle on the mountain holds you to it.

events.text: The lightning you send is exactly what {pw_vb_name} can take, and not a stroke more. It strips them to the bone of the soul and puts them back together. When the cloud clears they are still sitting in the snow, steaming, and they are not quite mortal any more. They look up and see you, really see you, and kneel.

choices.text: Raise them up into your Jade Court

effects.log: {pw_vb_name} climbs the last of the light into your court and kneels there. Below, every temple of {pw_world} lights at once.

choices.text: Ask them why they climbed

effects.log: "To see who made it all," {pw_vb_name} says. "And to ask if there was anything I could do." You give them a seat.

events.text: Nine strokes, ten, the last one the brightest. {pw_vb_name} takes every one of them, and with every one the mortal in them burns a little thinner and something else shows through. When it is over, {pw_vb_from} is gone, and what kneels on the mountain is a servant of heaven, tempered in your own fire.

choices.text: Give them a jade seal of office

effects.log: You press a seal of green jade into their hand. In {pw_world} they will be painted holding it, in a thousand temples.

choices.text: Give them a simple task first

effects.log: You send {pw_vb_name} to sweep the steps of your court. They do it without a word, and very well.

events.text: {pw_vb_name} was the first of {pw_world} to break the ceiling you made, and they did it in your lightning, and lived. They come up through the Void into the cold quiet of your heaven with their hair still smoking and their Dao, {pw_vb_dao}, burning clean in them, and kneel in the Jade Court, and wait for you to speak.

choices.text: Welcome them as kin

effects.log: "You are home," you tell them. {pw_vb_name} weeps, which immortals are not supposed to do. You let them.

choices.text: Welcome them as a servant

effects.log: "You serve now," you tell them. {pw_vb_name} bows to the floor. It is what they climbed for, or near enough.

choices.text: Welcome them as a rival to come

effects.log: You see in their eyes that one day they will want your seat. You give them one beside it, to watch them better.

events.text: {pw_vb_name} came through your lightning whole, tempered exactly as they should be. But your Jade Court is full, every seat in it taken by one who came before. They understand without being told. They bow to the full court, and to you, and step out through the Void into whatever lies beyond your sky.

choices.text: Give them your blessing for the road

effects.log: You give them a blessing for the road. Wherever they arrive, they will arrive lucky.

choices.text: Promise them a seat, one day

effects.log: You promise them a seat when one is empty. They smile as if they know how long a god takes to keep a promise.

events.text: The lightning was right; the timing was not. {pw_vb_name} kneels at the door of your heaven and finds every seat of the Jade Court filled. {pw_world} hears that its greatest mortal was found worthy, and sent on, and argues for a hundred years about whether that is an honour or a sorrow.

choices.text: Let the temples call it an honour

effects.log: The temples call it an honour. You wonder, privately, if they are right.

choices.text: Look over the servants you already have

effects.log: You look along the seats of your court and wonder which of them you would have given up. None, you decide. Not yet.

events.text: You did not answer. For two of your years the sky over {pw_world} cracked and groaned, and then one night, with nobody watching, {pw_vb_name} pushed through on their own. The temples of {pw_world} do not know whether their god was watching. Neither, if you are honest, do you.

choices.text: Look for them beyond the Void

effects.log: You look. They are already too far, walking a road you did not make. You wish them well.

choices.text: Tell yourself it is better so

effects.log: It is better so, you tell yourself. A god cannot be everywhere. The sky over the mountain stays cracked a while.

events.text: Word comes up to your heaven late, the way news reaches a house where nobody has been home. {pw_vb_name}, {pw_vb_from}, is gone: they broke the Void by themselves, while the god of {pw_world} was looking somewhere else.

choices.text: Leave a mark on the mountain where they sat

effects.log: You leave a ring of flowers in the snow that does not melt. The temples call it a sign. It is an apology.

choices.text: Watch the ceiling of the world more closely

effects.log: You turn your eye to the high places of {pw_world}. The next one, you will see coming.

events.text: You send {pw_vb_name} out of your heaven to spar with {pw_vb_foe}. The immortal laughs at them at first, a servant of a small god from a small world. By the hundredth exchange nobody is laughing. By the three hundredth, {pw_vb_foe} steps back, lowers their hands, and bows.

choices.text: Let them boast a little

effects.log: {pw_vb_name} comes home grinning and tells the whole court three times. You let them. It was well done.

choices.text: Ask them what they learned

effects.log: "That they were afraid of me by the end," {pw_vb_name} says. "And that I was afraid too." You nod. That is the lesson.

events.text: The spar between {pw_vb_name} and {pw_vb_foe} lasts a whole day of heaven, and the clouds for a thousand miles around are torn to ribbons by it. At sunset {pw_vb_name} stands alone on the field. In {pw_world} below, the people see the far sky light up all day and do not know they are watching their god win.

choices.text: Tell the temples of {pw_world}

effects.log: You let the temples of {pw_world} dream of it. In the morning every priest tells the same story, and they are right.

choices.text: Keep it in the court

effects.log: You keep it quiet. A court that wins should not need to say so. {pw_vb_name} stands taller for a year.

events.text: {pw_vb_foe} has not lost a spar in ten thousand years, they tell {pw_vb_name} before it begins. It is a long ten thousand years, and it ends on a bridge of cloud with {pw_vb_name} holding the immortal's own weapon and handing it politely back.

choices.text: Praise their manners

effects.log: "You gave it back," you say. "Of course," says {pw_vb_name}. "I am yours. I have to be polite." You laugh out loud.

choices.text: Praise their strength

effects.log: You praise their strength in front of the whole court. {pw_vb_name} goes red to the ears, as only a new immortal can.

events.text: {pw_vb_foe} is older than your whole world, and it shows. {pw_vb_name} fights well and long and is thrown, at last, down a stair of cloud into a heap at the bottom. They come home to your court on their own feet, slowly, and do not meet your eyes.

choices.text: Tend their wounds yourself

effects.log: You tend them with your own hands. "Next time," you say. {pw_vb_name} looks up at last.

choices.text: Tell them a loss is a lesson

effects.log: "A loss is the most expensive lesson there is," you tell them. "Do not waste it." They will not.

events.text: You feel it when {pw_vb_name} falls: a cold drop in your heaven, as if one of the lamps had gone out. They come back from {pw_vb_foe} with a note that is almost kind. The servant of your court is wounded, and ashamed, and will heal, slowly.

choices.text: Read the note aloud to the court

effects.log: The note says: "Good. Again in a hundred years." The court laughs, and so, after a moment, does {pw_vb_name}.

choices.text: Burn the note

effects.log: You burn the note. You will not have your court pitied. {pw_vb_name} watches the ash and says nothing.

events.text: It was too soon. You knew it, and sent {pw_vb_name} anyway, and {pw_vb_foe} taught them what an immortal of the old heavens is. They limp back into the Jade Court with their seal cracked and their pride worse.

choices.text: Say it was your mistake, not theirs

effects.log: "I sent you too soon," you say. It costs you something to say it. It is worth more to them than any victory.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let them heal

effects.log: You say nothing. Some wounds close better without a god looking at them.

events.text: One of your court is gone. {pw_vb_name}, who came up through your lightning and knelt to you, has gone back down into {pw_world} wearing your colours, and stands in your oldest temple, and tells the people the old god is dead. They are tempered in your own fire. The people believe them.

choices.text: Remember how you neglected them

effects.log: You remember the years you did not speak to your court. It is not an excuse for them. It is a reason.

choices.text: Swear that you will take your world back

effects.log: You swear it to the empty seat in your court. Below, the false god of {pw_world} looks up, and smiles.

events.text: The seat of {pw_vb_name} in your Jade Court is empty and cold, and the jade seal you gave them lies broken on it. Below, a voice that learned to speak with your authority is speaking to {pw_world} in your place.

choices.text: Pick up the broken seal

effects.log: You hold the two halves of the seal for a long time. Then you put them away, to give back one day, or to keep.

choices.text: Turn to the servants who stayed

effects.log: You look along the court at the ones who stayed. None of them will look back at you. You will have to earn that again.
